doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: North Beach in San Francisco, Mia Angelo and Miles down the street
summary: Hamilton and Brown recall the North Beach club strip where his group and Miles played neighboring clubs, and the hanging out with Mia Angelo, who lived on a barge.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Which two clubs were those? Was it the Black Hawk and the Jazz Workshop?
It was on the beach, now which one -­
You’re talking about in San Francisco?
Frisco, yeah, in North Beach.
Oh, in North Beach, yeah, yeah, right. So you had the Matador, you had Black Hawk, Jazz Workshop.
Yeah, too was at the Jazz Workshop.
The Hungry I.
Which was right up the road. Two or three doors down was another club. They were all on the same street.
I think the Matador was up there because I think Black Hawk was down at the Fillmore.
Hey man, speaking of that, did you know -- what was her name the -­
Mia Angelo?
Did you know Mia?
I met her but I didn’t know her back then.
You didn’t know her then.
I heard she was something else. She was a dancer and all kinds of stuff.

Hey, man, listen. You know I haven’t seen her. I’d like to see her. I really would like to see her again. I haven’t seen her since she became famous but man, you talk about hanging out. Remember Pony Poindexter? What was the name, Jimbo’s?
Yeah, he’s still there.
Yeah, man. Those were the days man. Mia lived on a barge.
Yeah, right, right. She called it a houseboat. So that was the scene up there.
Oh, man, we were the scene.
So you’re at one club and they’re at another club.
Oh, yeah, and Miles was at the next club. You know, but we were -- well all those records, Foreststorn Records, you know, we were hot. We got hot.
